		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<a name="Generaldescription"></a><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">General Description</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Landauer, Inc. is a Delaware corporation organized on December 22, 1987. As used herein, the &#x201C;Company</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201D; &#x201C;we</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201D; &#x201C;our</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201D; &#x201C;us&#x201D; or &#x201C;Landauer&#x201D; refers to Landauer, Inc. and its subsidiaries. The Company&#x2019;s </font><font style="display: inline;">common stock is</font><font style="display: inline;"> listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the</font><font style="display: inline;"> ticker</font><font style="display: inline;"> symbol </font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;">LDR.</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201D;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Landauer is a leading global provider of technical and analytical services to determine occupational and environmental radiation exposure</font><font style="display: inline;"> and</font><font style="display: inline;"> the leading domestic provider of outsourced medical physics services. </font><font style="display: inline;">The C</font><font style="display: inline;">ompany </font><font style="display: inline;">is organized into</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">three</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">reportable</font><font style="display: inline;"> business segments</font><font style="display: inline;">:</font><font style="display: inline;"> Radiation Measurement, Medical</font><font style="display: inline;"> Physics and </font><font style="display: inline;">Medical Products</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;"> The Medical Products business was divested in May 2016.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;"></font><font style="display: inline;">4</font><font style="display: inline;"></font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Radiation Measurement</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Radiation Measurement has b</font><font style="display: inline;">een the core business for over 6</font><font style="display: inline;">0 years. The Company has provided complete radiation dosimetry services to hospitals, medical and dental offices, universities, national laboratories, nuclear facilities and other industries in which radiation poses a potential threat to employees. Landauer&#x2019;s services include the manufacture of various types of radiation detection monitors, the distribution and collection of the monitors to and from customers, and the analysis and reporting of exposure findings. These services are provided to approximately </font><font style="display: inline;">1.8</font><font style="display: inline;"> million individuals globally. In addition to providing analytical services, the Company may</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">sell dosimetry detectors and reading equipment to large customers that want to manage their own dosimetry programs, or into smaller international markets in which it is not economical to establish a direct service.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The majority of Radiation Measurement revenues are realized from radiation measurement services and other services incidental to radiation dose measurement. The Company enters into agreements with customers to provide them with radiation measurement services, generally for a twelve-month period. Such agreements generally have a high renewal rate, resulting in customer relationships that are generally stable and recurring. As part of its services, the Company provides to its customers radiation detection badges, which are produced and owned by the Company. The badges are worn for a period selected by the customer (&#x201C;wear period&#x201D;), which is usually one, two, or three months in duration. At the end of the wear period, the badges are returned to the Company for analysis. The Company analyzes the badges that have been worn and provides the customer with a report indicating their radiation exposures. The Company recycles certain badge components for reuse, while also producing replacement badges on a continual basis.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company offers its service for measuring the dosages of x-ray, gamma radiation and other penetrating ionizing radiations to which the wearer has been exposed, primarily through badges, which contain OSL material, </font><font style="display: inline;">and</font><font style="display: inline;"> are worn by customer personnel. This technology is marketed under the trade names Luxel+</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:5pt;vertical-align:super;line-height:100%">&#xAE;</font><font style="display: inline;"> and InLight</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:5pt;vertical-align:super;line-height:100%">&#xAE;</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">A key component of the Company&#x2019;s dosimetry system is OSL crystal material. Radiation Measurement operates a crystal manufacturing facility in Stillwater, Oklahoma. The Company&#x2019;s base OSL material is manufactured utilizing a proprietary process to create aluminum oxide crystals in a unique structure that is able to retain charged electrons following the crystal&#x2019;s exposure to radiation.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Radiation Measurement&#x2019;s InLight dosimetry system provides in-house and commercial laboratories with the ability to provide in-house radiation measurement services using OSL technology. InLight services may involve a customer acquiring dosimetry devices as well as analytical reading equipment from the Company. The system is based on the Company&#x2019;s proprietary technology and instruments. The InLight system allows customers the flexibility to tailor their precise dosimetry needs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Radiation Measurement&#x2019;s </font><font style="display: inline;">RadWatch and RadLight</font><font style="display: inline;"> system provides the military and first responder user with a portable, field-ready option for tactical radiation mo</font><font style="display: inline;">nitoring using OSL technology. </font><font style="display: inline;">RadWatch and RadLight</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">are</font><font style="display: inline;"> offered through a </font><font style="display: inline;">joint venture</font><font style="display: inline;"> with Yamasato, Fujiwara, Higa &amp; Associates, Inc. (&#x201C;YFH&#x201D;)</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> doing business as Aqu</font><font style="display: inline;">ila Group</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> a small business supplier to the International Atomic Energy Agency and the U.S. Military. The Company provides dosimetry parts to Aquila Group for their military contract</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Rad</font><font style="display: inline;">Watch</font><font style="display: inline;"> and RadLight</font><font style="display: inline;"> solution fulfills a recognized gap for acquiring a legal dose of record for radiation emergency response teams.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Other radiation measurement-related services augment the basic radiation measurement services that the Company offers, providing administrative and informational tools to customers for the management of their radiation safety programs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Medical Physics</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Medical physics services are provided through the Company&#x2019;s Landauer Medical Physics (&#x201C;LMP&#x201D;) division. </font><font style="display: inline;">In November 2009, Landauer completed its first LMP acquisition by acquiring Global Physics Solutions, Inc. (&#x201C;GPS&#x201D;). </font><font style="display: inline;">Landauer</font><font style="display: inline;"> acquired five</font><font style="display: inline;"> regional practices</font><font style="display: inline;"> from 2010 to</font><font style="display: inline;"> 2012 to augment the LMP operations. </font><font style="display: inline;">With primary offices in Illinois and New York, LMP has operations throughout the United States (&#x201C;U.S.&#x201D;).</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;"></font><font style="display: inline;">5</font><font style="display: inline;"></font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">The Company uses LMP as a platform to expand into the medical physics services market, serving domestic hospitals, radiation therapy centers and imaging centers. LMP is the leading nationwide service provider of clinical physics support, equipment commissioning and accreditation support and imaging equipment testing. Clinical physics support is provided by medical physicists, who individually focus on either imaging or therapeutic medical physics. Imaging physicists are concerned primarily with the radiation delivered by imaging equipment, image quality and compliance with safe practices in nuclear pharmacies. Therapeutic physicists are concerned with the safe delivery of radiation in cancer treatment. Therapeutic physicists contribute to the development of therapeutic techniques, collaborate with radiation oncologists to design treatment plans, and monitor equipment and procedures to ensure that cancer patients receive the prescribed dose of radiation to the correct location. Both specialties are aligned with critical treatment trends in the continued increase in utilization of radiation for the diagnosis and treatment of disease. The ability to target treatments and reduce the impact of surgical procedures is often aided by imaging and therapeutic techniques. </font><font style="display: inline;">The Company reports the operating results of LMP in the Medical Physics reporting segment.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Medical Products</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Landauer divested the Medical Products busines</font><font style="display: inline;">s &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">i</font><font style="display: inline;">n May 2016. The Medical Produ</font><font style="display: inline;">cts business was a</font><font style="display: inline;"> provider of high quality medical consumable accessories used in radiology, radiation therapy, and ima</font><font style="display: inline;">ge guided surgical procedures. </font><font style="display: inline;">Medical products </font><font style="display: inline;">range</font><font style="display: inline;">d</font><font style="display: inline;"> from consumables used with magnetic resonance imaging (&#x201C;MRI&#x201D;), computed tomography (&#x201C;CT&#x201D;), and mammography technologies to highly engineered passive reflective markers used during ima</font><font style="display: inline;">ge guided surgical procedures.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Landauer believes that its business is largely dependent upon the Company&#x2019;s technical competence, the quality, reliability and price of its services and products, and its prompt and responsive service.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">For most radiation dosimetry laboratories operating around the world, the laboratory must maintain accreditation with a regulatory body to provide the user with a formal record of dose &#x2013; a process that is expensive and time consuming. By combining the implementation of an InLight system in the laboratory and &#x201C;dose of record&#x201D; determination by Landauer or a Landauer affiliated and accredited facility, the user can provide its workers with the periodic radiation safety management infrastructure without the need to maintain its own accreditation. Additionally, dosimetry management software options provide the ability to measure the incremental radiation dose of workers at regular intervals over long periods of time.</font>

Landauer internally produces certain of its require</font><font style="display: inline;">d materials</font><font style="display: inline;">, such as OSL detector materials and plastic badge holders. All crystal materials used in the Company&#x2019;s OSL technology are produced at the Company&#x2019;s crystal manufacturing facility in Stillwater, Oklahoma. The InLight dosimetry system and its components are manufactured by a Japanese company under an exclusive agreement. The Company sources the </font><font style="display: inline;">RadWatch and RadLight</font><font style="display: inline;"> analytical instrument sold for military and emergency radiological response applications from </font><font style="display: inline;">its joint venture partner, </font><font style="display: inline;">YFH</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> on a sole source basis. </font><font style="display: inline;">The Company</font><font style="display: inline;"> sources a key component of its medical products from a sole supplier. If the Company were to lose availability of its Stillwater facility or materials from </font><font style="display: inline;">its</font><font style="display: inline;"> sole supplier</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> due to a fire, natural disaster or other disruptions, such loss could have a material adverse effect on the Company and its operations.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<a name="competition"></a><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">Competition</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In the U.S., the Company competes against a number of dosimetry service providers. One of these providers is a division of Mirion Technologies,</font><font style="display: inline;"> Inc.,</font><font style="display: inline;"> a significant competitor with substantial resources. Other competitors in the U.S. that provide dosimetry services tend to be smaller companies, some of which operate on a regional basis. Most government agencies in the U.S., such as the Department of Energy and Department of Defense, have their own in-house radiation measurement services, as do many large private nuclear power plants. Outside of the U.S., radiation measurement activities are conducted by a combination of private entities and government agencies. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">The Company competes on the basis of advanced technologies, competent execution of these technologies, the quality, reliability and price of its services, and its prompt and responsive performance. The Company&#x2019;s InLight dosimetry system competes with other dosimetry systems based on the technical advantages of OSL methods combined with an integrated systems approach featuring comprehensive software, automation and value.</font><font style="display: inline;"> Changing market demand for combining active and passive dosimetry will be redefining the competition and the opportunities going forward.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Medical </font><font style="display: inline;">P</font><font style="display: inline;">hysics outsourced services represent</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">a large fragmented market where LMP has many small competitors. In addition, many facilities directly employ full-time physicists as an alternative for obtaining services from an outsourced provider. LMP competes with other outsourced medical physicists by having responsive regional practices that are backed by the safety, stability and standards of a global company. LMP offers a complementary alternative for clients who require support for their full-time staff in meeting patient care needs.</font>
		</p>

			<a name="researchanddevelopment"></a><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">Research and Development</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;s technological expertise has been an important factor in its growth. The Company regularly pursues product improvements to maintain its technical position. The development of OSL dosimetry, announced in 1994, was funded by the Company in its collaborative effort with Battelle </font><font style="display: inline;">Memorial Institute </font><font style="display: inline;">and OSU. The Company commercialized this technology beginning in 1998 and has converted most of its customers to the technology.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;Current research efforts are focused on developing the Verifii</font><font style="display: inline;font-size:5pt;vertical-align:super;line-height:100%">TM</font><font style="display: inline;"> digital dosimetry platform (&#x201C;Verifii&#x201D;), a wireless wearable dosimeter with built-in compliance.&nbsp;&nbsp;Verifii dosimeters will connect, collect, and display exposure levels for frequent readings on laptops and mobile devices and will provide data to radiation safety officers for timely review and action.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Verifii dashboards will provide instant access to enterprise data or individual exposure readings.</font>

Current research efforts are</font><font style="display: inline;"> focused on</font><font style="display: inline;"> radiology products, which reduce radiation exposure to physicians and patients, as well as products that increase the accuracy of imaging by using reference markers.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Domestic and International Regulations</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company manufactures and markets products that are medical devices subject to regulation by numerous government agencies, including the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (&#x201C;FDA&#x201D;), and similar regulatory bodies outside the U.S. FDA regulations</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> and similar regulations outside the U.S., govern the following activities that the Company performs and will continue to perform: product design and development; document and purchasing controls; production and process controls; acceptance controls; product testing; product manufacturing; product safety; product labeling; product storage; recordkeeping; complaint handling; pre-market clearance; advertising and promotion; and product sales and distribution.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">FDA pre-market clearance and approval requirements.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;Unless an exemption applies, each medical device the Company wishes to commercially distribute in the U.S. will require either prior 510(k) clearance or pre-market approval from the FDA. The FDA classifies medical devices into one of three classes. Devices deemed to pose lower risks are placed in either class&nbsp;I or II, which requires the manufacturer to submit to the FDA a pre-market notification to commercially distribute the device. This process is generally known as 510(k) clearance. Some low- risk devices are exempted from this requirement. Devices deemed by the FDA to pose the greatest risks, such as life-sustaining, life-supporting or implantable devices, or devices deemed not substantially equivalent to a previously cleared 510(k) device, are placed in class&nbsp;III and require pre-market approval. All of the Company&#x2019;s current products are either class I or class&nbsp;II devices. </font>
		</p>

and procedures related to the marketing of medical devices ex</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">ist and must be complied with. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">For example, in the </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">European Union (</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">EU</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#x201D;)</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, medical devices must meet minimum standards of performance, safety and quality, and follow one of several conformity assessment routes, depe</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">nding on their classification. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Some of these conformity assessment routes involve an assessment and cer</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">tification by a notified body. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Manufacturers indicate compliance with applicable EU medical device regulations by preparing a Declaration of Conformity and by applying a CE Mark to their medical devices before placing them on t</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">he market in the EU. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">An appropriate quality system is required and manufacturers must report certain product and safety-related information to government agencies </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">of individual EU Member States.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> Various penalties and sanctions exist in different EU Member States for non-compliance with EU medical device regulations and related requirements, for example with respect to data protection and privacy.</font>

The False Claims Act imposes liability on any person or entity that submits or causes to be submitted a claim to the Federal government that he or she knows (or should know) is false. Its success depends largely on its general ability to attract, develop, motivate and retain highly skilled licensed medical physicists. Further, the Company must successfully maintain the right mix of physicists with relevant experience and skill sets as it expands into new service offerings, and as the market evolves. The loss of a significant number of its physicists, the inability to attract, hire, develop, train and retain additional skilled personnel, or not maintaining the right mix of professionals could have a serious negative effect on the Company, including its ability to manage, staff and successfully complete its existing engagements and obtain new engagements. Qualified physicists are in great demand, and the Company faces significant competition for both senior and junior physicists with the requisite credentials and experience. The Company&#x2019;s principal competition for talent comes from other outsourced medical physicist firms, hospitals and free-standing radiation therapy centers. Many of these competitors may be able to offer significantly greater compensation and benefits or more attractive lifestyle choices, career paths or geographic locations than those of the Company. Therefore, the Company may not be successful in attracting and retaining the skilled physicists it requires to conduct and expand its operations successfully. In addition, the level and effect of radiation being administered by certain radiation equipment is also attracting increased scrutiny and giving rise to patient safety claims. Many of these lawsuits involve large claims and substantial defense costs. As the Company increases its presence in the healthcare industry, through the Medical Physics business, it could be exposed to litigation or subject to fines, penalties or suspension of services relating to the compliance with regulatory requirements</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Cambria;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-size:11pt;">&#xFEFF;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Book Antiqua;line-height:100%;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">On November 22, 2016, Gilead Capital LP (together with its affiliates, &#x201C;Gilead&#x201D;) filed a Schedule 13D with the SEC, reporting a 5% ownership of the Company&#x2019;s outstanding shares of Common Stock. On November 28, 2016, Gilead filed a Schedule 13D/A (Amendment No. 1) with the SEC, suggesting that it intended to run a slate of directors in opposition to the Board&#x2019;s nominees at the 2017 annual meeting of </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">the </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:Times New Roman;">Company&#x2019;s stockholders. If Gilead nominates a slate of directors, and does not subsequently withdraw its nominations, a proxy contest is likely to occur and it may require us to incur legal fees and proxy solicitation expenses in addition to those normally expended for a solicitation. The perceived uncertainties as to our future direction also could affect the market price and volatility of our securities.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Comparison of the Fiscal Years Ended September 30, 201</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">6</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;"> and 201</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">5</font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Revenues for fiscal </font><font style="display: inline;">2016 were $149.2</font><font style="display: inline;"> million</font><font style="display: inline;">, a decrease of $2.1 million, or 1.4% compared to revenues of </font><font style="display: inline;">$</font><font style="display: inline;">151.3 million</font><font style="display: inline;"> for fiscal 2015.</font><font style="display: inline;"> Revenues in the Radiation Measurement segment decreased </font><font style="display: inline;">$</font><font style="display: inline;">1.8</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, which was primarily due to </font><font style="display: inline;">the Radon business that was divested in September 2015, resulting in a $4.6 million&nbsp;reduction in revenues.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, unfavorable foreign currency translation rates reduced revenues by $2.0 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;Domestic Radiation Measurement services revenues Revenues in the Medical Products segment increased $0.6 million primarily due to the full year impact from a modest acquisition in December 2013.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;">Gross margin for fiscal 2015 was 52.0% compared to 52.2% for fiscal 2014. Gross margin in the Radiation Measurement segment increased by 1.2%, due to an improved mix of higher margin service revenues versus lower margin product revenues. Gross margin in the Medical Physics segment increased by 0.3%, primarily due to an </font>

Gross margin in the Medical Products segment decreased by 1.3%, due to continued Spherz pricing pressure.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;">Selling, general and administrative expenses for fiscal 2015 were $54.0 million, a decrease of $0.9 million, or 1.7%, compared to $54.9 million for fiscal 2014, primarily due to lower amortization expense and lower research and development expenses, partially offset by higher professional fees and sales and marketing spending. Amortization expense decreased $1.8 million as a result of impairments recorded in fiscal 2014 to reduce the carrying value of intangible assets in the Medical Products segment. Changes in foreign currency rates resulted in a $1.6 million decrease in expenses. Research and development expenses decreased $1.2 million due to early-stage design services incurred in fiscal 2014 to support the Verifii next generation dosimetry platform that were not present in fiscal 2015. Audit, legal and other professional fees increased $2.0 million </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">in the current year primarily </font><font style="display: inline;">associated with the fiscal 2014 Form 10-K restatement and accounting control issues. Sales and marketing spending increased approximately $1.5 million to support growth initiatives in the Radiation Measurement segment.</font>

The increase in operating income was primarily due to the $62.2 million goodwill and other intangible assets impairment charge recorded in fiscal 2014 that was not present in fiscal 2015 and a $2.8 million reduction in acquisition, reorganization and nonrecurring costs.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 11pt"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">Critical Accounting Policies</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;"> and Estimates</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The preparation of financial statements in conformity with </font><font style="display: inline;">U.S. GAAP </font><font style="display: inline;">requires that management </font><font style="display: inline;">apply accounting policies and </font><font style="display: inline;">make estimates </font><font style="display: inline;">and assumptions </font><font style="display: inline;">that affect the results of operations and the amounts of assets and liabilities reported in the financial statements</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> as well as related disclosures. </font><font style="display: inline;">Management discusses these policies, estimates and assumptions with its </font><font style="display: inline;">accounting and disclosure governance committee on a regular basis and provides periodic updates on management decisions to the </font><font style="display: inline;">A</font><font style="display: inline;">udit </font><font style="display: inline;">C</font><font style="display: inline;">ommittee of the Landauer </font><font style="display: inline;">B</font><font style="display: inline;">oard of </font><font style="display: inline;">D</font><font style="display: inline;">irectors. </font><font style="display: inline;">Critical accounting policies are those that are most important to the portrayal of a company&#x2019;s financial condition and results</font><font style="display: inline;"> of operations</font><font style="display: inline;">, and that require management&#x2019;s most difficult, subjective or complex judgments, often as a result of the need to make estimates about the effect of matters that are inherently uncertain. </font><font style="display: inline;">We believe that</font><font style="display: inline;"> the application of</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">the accounting policies </font><font style="display: inline;">described below</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">require significant judgments and estimates on the part of mana</font><font style="display: inline;">gement </font><font style="display: inline;">in the preparation of the Company&#x2019;s financial statements and accompanying notes.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">For a summary of our significant accounting policies, including the accounting poli</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">cies discussed below, see Note 1</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> to the Consolidated Financial Statements.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Revenue Recognition and Deferred Contract Revenue</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The majority of Radiation Measurement revenues are realized from radiation measurement services and other services incidental to radiation dose measurement. The measuring and monitoring services provided by the Company to its customers are of a subscription nature and are continuous. The Company views its business in the Radiation Measurement segment as services provided to customers over a period of time and the wear period is the period over which those services are provided. Badge production, wearing of badges, badge analysis, and report preparation are integral to the benefit that the Company provides to its customers. These services are provided to customers on an agreed-upon recurring basis (monthly, bi-monthly, quarterly, semi-annually or annually) that the custom</font><font style="display: inline;">er chooses for the wear period.</font><font style="display: inline;"> Revenue is recognized on a straight-line basis</font><font style="display: inline;"> over the wear period.</font><font style="display: inline;"> Revenues are recognized over the periods in which the customers wear the badges irrespective of whether invo</font><font style="display: inline;">iced in advance or in arrears. </font><font style="display: inline;">To a lesser degree, the Company provides equipment and sells badges to smaller distrib</font><font style="display: inline;">utors and joint ventures. </font><font style="display: inline;">Radiation Measurement segment product revenues are recognized upon delivery of goods when title and risk of loss pass to customers.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company, through its Medical Physics segment, offers full scope medical physics services to hospitals and radiation therapy centers. Services offered include, but are not limited to, clinical physics support in radiation oncology, commissioning services, special projects support and imaging physics services. Delivery of medical physics services can be of a contracted, recurring nature or as a discrete project with a defined service outcome. Recurring services often are provided on the customer</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s premises by a full-time employee or fraction of a full-time employee. These services are recognized as revenue on a straight-line basis over the life of the contract unless there is another discernable pattern as the services are rendered. Fee for service revenue is recognized when the service is delivered.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Contracted services are billed on an agreed-upon recurring basis, either in advance or arrears of the service being delivered. Customers may be billed monthly, quarterly, or at some other regular interval over the contracted period. The amounts recorded as deferred</font><font style="display: inline;"> contract</font><font style="display: inline;"> revenue represent invoiced amounts in advance of delivery of the service. Management believes that the amount of deferred contract revenue fairly represents remaining business activity with customers invoiced in advance. Fee for service revenue is typically associated with much shorter contract periods, or with discrete individual projects, and revenue is recognized upon completion of the project and customer acceptance.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Medical Products business was divested in May 2016. </font><font style="display: inline;">The Medical Products segment offer</font><font style="display: inline;">ed</font><font style="display: inline;"> a broad product portfolio ranging from consumables used with MRI, CT, and mammography technologies to highly engineered consumable passive reflective markers used during image guided surgery procedures. The Medical Products segment recognize</font><font style="display: inline;">d</font><font style="display: inline;"> revenues upon shipment or delivery of goods when title and risk of loss pass to customers.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;"></font><font style="display: inline;">33</font><font style="display: inline;"></font>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Property, Plant &amp; Equipment and Other Assets</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Maintenance and repairs are charged to expense and renewals and betterments are capitalized. Plant and equipment and other assets, primarily dosimetry badges, are recorded at cost and are depreciated or amortized on a straight-line basis over the estimated useful lives, which are primarily 30 years for buildings, 3 to 8 years for equipment, 5 to 10 years for internal software and 30 months to 8 years for </font><font style="display: inline;">dosimetry devices</font><font style="display: inline;">. The Company assesses the carrying value and the remaining useful lives of its property, plant, equipment and other assets when events or circumstances indicate the carrying value may not be recoverable or the estimated useful life may no longer be appropriate. Factors that could trigger this review</font><font style="display: inline;"> include competitive conditions, government regulati</font><font style="display: inline;">ons and technological changes. </font><font style="display: inline;">Any change in the carrying value or estimated useful lives of property, plant, equipment and other assets could materially impact the Company&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">results of operation</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> financial position and</font><font style="display: inline;"> liquidity.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;background-color:yellow;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company capitalizes costs of software which is acquired, internally developed, or modified solely to meet</font><font style="display: inline;"> the Company&#x2019;s internal needs. </font><font style="display: inline;">Internal and external costs incurred to develop internal-use computer software during the application development stage are capitalized. Costs incurred during the preliminary project stage as well as training costs and maintenance costs during the post implementation-operation stage are expensed. Capitalized costs of software amounted to </font><font style="display: inline;">$0.4 million and </font><font style="display: inline;">$</font><font style="display: inline;">0.7</font><font style="display: inline;"> million for fiscal 201</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">and 201</font><font style="display: inline;">5</font><font style="display: inline;">, respectively.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company&#x2019;s intangible assets include purchased customer lists, licenses, patents, trademarks, tradenames and goodwill. Purchased customer lists are recorded at cost and are amortized on a straight-line basis over estimated useful lives, which range from 4 to 15 years. Patents and licenses are also recorded at cost and are amortized on a straight-line basis over their useful lives, which range from 10 to 20 years. Tradenames have both definite lives up to 10 years and indefinite lives. The Company acquired goodwill primarily from its acquisitions of Landauer-Europe, SAPRA-Landauer, LMP </font><font style="display: inline;">and IZI</font><font style="display: inline;"> Medical Products, LLC </font><font style="display: inline;">(which was part of the Medical Products business divested in May 2016)</font><font style="display: inline;"> as well as other smaller investments. Goodwill has an indefinite life.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Goodwill and certain intangible assets with indefinite lives are reviewed annually for impairment and more frequently if </font><font style="display: inline;">an event occurs or circumstances change that would require the Company to perform an interim review</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;"> The Company has three</font><font style="display: inline;"> reporting units</font><font style="display: inline;">: Radiation Measurement; Medical Physics; and Medical Products.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Goodwill impairment testing first requires a comparison between the carrying value and fair value of a reporting </font><font style="display: inline;">unit</font><font style="display: inline;"> with associated goodwill. Carrying value is based on the assets and liabilities associated with the operations of that reporting </font><font style="display: inline;">unit</font><font style="display: inline;">. The Company estimates the fair value of the reporting </font><font style="display: inline;">units </font><font style="display: inline;">using the income approach and the market approach. If the Company believes that the fair value of a reporting </font><font style="display: inline;">unit </font><font style="display: inline;">exceeds its carrying value by a substantial margin, the Company may perform a qualitative analysis instead.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">If the fair value of a </font><font style="display: inline;">reporting unit</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">exceeds its carrying amount, goodwill of the </font><font style="display: inline;">reporting unit</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">is considered not to be impaired and the second step of the impairment test is unnecessary. If the carrying amount of the </font><font style="display: inline;">reporting unit</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">exceeds its fair value, the second step of the goodwill impairment test is performed to measure the amount of the impairment loss, if any. The second step of the goodwill impairment test compares the implied fair value of the </font><font style="display: inline;">reporting unit&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">goodwill with the carrying amount of that goodwill. If the carrying amount of the </font><font style="display: inline;">reporting unit&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">goodwill exceeds the implied fair value of that goodwill, an impairment loss is recognized in an amount equal to that excess. The implied fair value of goodwill is determined in the same manner as the amount of goodwill recognized in a business combination. That is, the fair value of the </font><font style="display: inline;">reporting unit</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">is allocated to all of the assets and liabilities of that </font><font style="display: inline;">reporting unit</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">(including any unrecognized intangible assets) as if the </font><font style="display: inline;">reporting unit</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">had been acquired in a business combination, and the fair value of the </font><font style="display: inline;">reporting unit </font><font style="display: inline;">was the purchase price paid to acquire the</font><font style="display: inline;"> reporting unit</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;line-height:110%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;"></font><font style="display: inline;">34</font><font style="display: inline;"></font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;line-height:110%;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company estimated the fair value of the Radiation Measurement</font><font style="display: inline;"> and</font><font style="display: inline;"> Medical Physics reporting </font><font style="display: inline;">units </font><font style="display: inline;">as of September 30, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;"> using the income approach and the market approach, and no impairment charges resulted. In the income approach, the Company utilized a discounted cash flow analysis, which involved estimating the expected after-tax cash flows that will be generated by the reporting segments and then discounting these cash flows to present value reflecting the relevant risks associated with the reporting </font><font style="display: inline;">unit</font><font style="display: inline;"> and the time value of money. This approach requires the use of significant estimates and assumptions, including long-term projections of future cash flows, market conditions, discount rates reflecting the risk inherent in future cash flows, revenue growth, perpetual growth rates and profitability, among others. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The market approach is primarily comprised of comparable companies. This approach compares the subject segment to selected reasonably similar companies whose securities are actively traded in the public markets. For companies providing services similar to those provided by the Company, the income and market approaches will generally provide the most reliable indications of value because the value of such companies is more dependent on their ability to generate earnings than on the value of the individual assets.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company completed an impairment test for Medical Products as of June 30, 2014 when it became apparent that anticipated revenue and profitability trends in Medical Products were not being achieved to the extent forecasted. Based on the testing performed, the Company recorded a non-cash impairment charge of $62.2 million, of which $41.4 million related to goodwill and $20.8 million related to intangible assets for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2014.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;The Medical Products business was divested in May 2016.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Intangible assets represent purchased assets that lack physical substance but can be distinguished from goodwill. The Company uses valuation techniques in estimating the initial fair value of acquired intangible assets. These valuations are primarily based on the present value of the estimated net cash flows expected to be derived from the intangible assets, discounted for assumptions such as future customer attrition. The Company evaluates intangible assets for impairment annually or whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of the assets may not be recoverable. Therefore, changes such as higher or earlier-than-expected customer attrition or obsolescence of technology may result in higher future amortization charges or an impairment charge for intangible assets. See Note </font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;"> to the Consolidated Financial Statements for additional information regarding the value of goodwill and other intangible assets.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Income Taxes</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company estimates the income tax provision for income taxes that are currently payable and records deferred </font><font style="display: inline;">income </font><font style="display: inline;">tax assets and liabilities for the temporary differences in tax consequences between the financial statements and tax returns. Temporary differences result from, among other events, revenues, expenses, gains, or losses that are included in taxable income of an earlier or later year than the year in which they are recognized in financial statement income. These deferred </font><font style="display: inline;">income </font><font style="display: inline;">tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income</font><font style="display: inline;"> in the years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled. To the extent that deferred</font><font style="display: inline;"> income</font><font style="display: inline;"> tax assets will not likely be recovered from future taxable income, a valuation allowance is established ag</font><font style="display: inline;">ainst such deferred </font><font style="display: inline;">income </font><font style="display: inline;">tax assets. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The Company has no indefinite reinvestment assertions on its foreign earnings and profits. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Management exercises significant judgment in the valuation of its current and deferred </font><font style="display: inline;">income </font><font style="display: inline;">tax assets and liabilities. The Company recognizes the financial statement effects of its tax positions in its current and deferred </font><font style="display: inline;">income </font><font style="display: inline;">tax assets and liabilities when it is more likely than not that the position will be sustained upon examination by a taxing authority. Management considers, among other factors, the Company&#x2019;s current and past performance, the market environment in </font><font style="display: inline;">which the Company operates, and tax planning strategies. Further, the Company provides for income tax issues not yet resolved with federal, state, local, and foreign tax authorities. The Company assesses and updates its tax positions when significant changes in circumstances occur, which may cause a change in judgment about the likelihood of realizing the deferred items. Changes in circumstances or judgment about tax positions may cause a change in the Com</font><font style="display: inline;">pany&#x2019;s uncertain tax position. </font><font style="display: inline;">Variations in the actual outcome of these future tax consequences could materially impact the Company&#x2019;s results of operations</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">financial position</font><font style="display: inline;"> and liquidity</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">S</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">ee Note </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">9</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> to the Consolidated Financial Statements</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">for additional</font><font style="display: inline;"> information regar</font><font style="display: inline;">ding </font><font style="display: inline;">the Company&#x2019;s income taxes</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Defined Benefit Pension and Other Postretirement Benefit Plans</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The defined benefit pension and other postretirement benefit plan</font><font style="display: inline;">s were frozen as of March 2009.</font><font style="display: inline;"> The pension expenses and benefit obligations recorded for the Company&#x2019;s defined benefit plans are depen</font><font style="display: inline;">dent on actuarial assumptions. </font><font style="display: inline;">These assumptions include discount rates, expected return on plan assets, interest costs, expected compensation increases, benefits earned, mortality rates, and other factors. Management review</font><font style="display: inline;">s the plan assumptions on an annual basis to ensure that the most current, relevant information is considered. During fiscal 2014, the Company adopted the RP-2014 mortality tables and the Mortality Improvement Scale MP-2014 published by the Society of Actuaries&#x2019; Retirement Plans Experience Committee. </font><font style="display: inline;">The pension expense for fiscal year 2014 was</font><font style="display: inline;"> derived based on the 2013 IRS Static Mortality table, while the pension expense for fiscal year</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> 201</font><font style="display: inline;">6 and 2015</font><font style="display: inline;"> was derived based on the RP-2014 Mortality Table with Scale MP, to reflect future mortality improvements. </font><font style="display: inline;">If actual results vary considerably from those that are expected or if future changes are made</font><font style="display: inline;"> to these assumptions, the amounts recognized for these plans could change significantly. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The weighted-average assumed discount rates used to determine plan expenses </font><font style="display: inline;">were 4.</font><font style="display: inline;">1</font><font style="display: inline;">5</font><font style="display: inline;">%</font><font style="display: inline;"> for pension </font><font style="display: inline;">benefits </font><font style="display: inline;">and </font><font style="display: inline;">3.4</font><font style="display: inline;">3</font><font style="display: inline;">% for </font><font style="display: inline;">other benefits in fiscal 201</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;">, compared to</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">4.14% for pension benefits and 3.40% for other benefits in fiscal 2015</font><font style="display: inline;">. For fiscal 201</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;"> expense, the </font><font style="display: inline;">expected </font><font style="display: inline;">long-term rate of return of plan assets </font><font style="display: inline;">was 6.50</font><font style="display: inline;">%, unchanged from fiscal 201</font><font style="display: inline;">5</font><font style="display: inline;">. In establishing the rate, management considered the historical rates of return and the current and planned asset classes of </font><font style="display: inline;">the plan investment portfolio. </font><font style="display: inline;">The weighted-average discount rate used to determine benefit obligations at September&nbsp;30, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;"> was </font><font style="display: inline;">3.38</font><font style="display: inline;">%, 3.</font><font style="display: inline;">04</font><font style="display: inline;">%, </font><font style="display: inline;">3.30</font><font style="display: inline;">% and 2.</font><font style="display: inline;">35</font><font style="display: inline;">% for Pension, Key Executive SERP, Manager SERP and Directors plans, respectively, under &#x201C;Pension Benefits&#x201D; in the &#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;">Employee</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Benefit Plans&#x201D; footnote of this Annual Re</font><font style="display: inline;">port on Form 10-K. </font><font style="display: inline;">The weighted-average discount rate used to determine benefit obligations under &#x201C;Other Benefits&#x201D; wa</font><font style="display: inline;">s &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">2.76</font><font style="display: inline;">% at September 30, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Comparatively, the weighted-average discount rate</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> used to determine benefit obligations at September 30, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">5</font><font style="display: inline;"> was </font><font style="display: inline;">4.15</font><font style="display: inline;">%, 3.</font><font style="display: inline;">80</font><font style="display: inline;">%, 4.</font><font style="display: inline;">06</font><font style="display: inline;">% and 2.98</font><font style="display: inline;">% for Pension, Key Executive SERP, Manager SERP and Directors plans, respectively, </font><font style="display: inline;">and t</font><font style="display: inline;">he weighted-average discount rate used to determine benefit obligations under &#x201C;Other Benefits&#x201D; wa</font><font style="display: inline;">s &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">3.4</font><font style="display: inline;">3</font><font style="display: inline;">% at September 30, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">5</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company recognizes on its balance sheet the amount by which the projected benefit obligations of its defined benefit plans exceed the fair value of plan assets. Subsequent changes in the funded status of the plans as a </font><font style="display: inline;">result of future transactions and events, amortization of previously unrecognized costs, and changes to actuarial assumptions are recognized as an asset or a liability and amortized as components of net periodic pension cost or accumulated other comprehensive income. An increase or decrease in the assumptions or economic events outside of management&#x2019;s control could have a material effect on the Company&#x2019;s results of operations or financial condition. </font><font style="display: inline;">S</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">ee Note 1</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">2</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> to the Consolidated Financial Statements</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">for additional</font><font style="display: inline;"> information regar</font><font style="display: inline;">ding </font><font style="display: inline;">these </font><font style="display: inline;">benefit </font><font style="display: inline;">plans</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Stock-Based Compensation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company measures and recognizes compensation cost at fair value for all stock-based awards, net of the estimated impact of forfeited</font><font style="display: inline;"> awards. The Company has not granted stock options subsequent to fiscal 2005. The fair values of options were estimated using a Black-Scholes option pricing model. In addition to stock options, key employees and/or non-employee directors are eligible to receive performance shares and restricted stock. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">U</font><font style="display: inline;">nder the Company&#x2019;s 2016 Incentive Compensation Plan adopted in February 2016</font><font style="display: inline;">, the fair value of </font><font style="display: inline;">the</font><font style="display: inline;"> restricted stock </font><font style="display: inline;">and performance shares </font><font style="display: inline;">granted under the new plan is based on the Company&#x2019;s closing stock price on the grant date. </font><font style="display: inline;">Stock-based c</font><font style="display: inline;">ompensation expense for restricted stock is</font><font style="display: inline;"> cliff vested and</font><font style="display: inline;"> recognized ratably over the vesting period.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">The terms of performance share awards allow the recipients of such awards to earn a variable number of shares based on the achievement of the performance</font><font style="display: inline;"> goals specified in the awards. </font><font style="display: inline;">Stock-based compensation expense associated with performance share awards is </font><font style="display: inline;">cliff vested and </font><font style="display: inline;">recognized based on management&#x2019;s best estimates of the achievement of the performance goals specified in such awards and the resulting number of shares that are expected to be earned. The Company evaluates on a quarterly basis the progress towards </font><font style="display: inline;">achieving the performance criteria. The cumulative effect on current and prior periods of a change in the estimated number of performance share awards expected to be earned is recognized as compensation cost or as a reduction of cost in the period of the revised estimate. The Company also retains the discretion to make additional awards to executives at other times for recr</font><font style="display: inline;">uiting or retention purposes.</font><font style="display: inline;"> Stock-based compensation for these awards can be either cliff or graded vested depending on the agreement, and recognized ratably over the vesting period.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;"></font><font style="display: inline;">36</font><font style="display: inline;"></font>
