		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">Forfeitures of awards are estimated at the time of grant and stock-based compensation cost is recognized only for those awards expected to vest. The Company uses historical experience to estimate projected forfeitures. The Company recognizes the cumulative effect on current and prior periods of a change in the forfeiture rate, or actual forfeitures, as compensation cost or as a reduction of cost in the period of the revision. If revisions are made to management&#x2019;s assumptions and estimates or if actual results vary considerably from those that are expected, stock-based compensation expense could change</font><font style="display: inline;"> significantly, impacting the Company&#x2019;s results of operations or financial condition.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;S</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">ee Note 1</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">4</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> to the Consolidated Financial Statements</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">for additional</font><font style="display: inline;"> information regar</font><font style="display: inline;">ding </font><font style="display: inline;">the Company&#x2019;s stock-based awards</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>

			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">Inflation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company strives to reflect the inflationary impact of materials, labor and other operating costs and expenses in its prices. The market for the services and products that the Company offers, however, is highly competitive, and in some cases has limited the ability of the Company to offset inflationary cost increases.</font>
		</p>

			<a name="QandQmarketrisk"></a><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">Item 7A.&nbsp;&nbsp;Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company is exposed to market risk, including changes in foreign currency exchange rates. The financial statements of the Company&#x2019;s international subsidiaries are remeasured into U.S. dollars </font><font style="display: inline;">monthly </font><font style="display: inline;">using the U.S. dollar as the reporting currency. To date, the market risk associated with foreign currency exchange rates has not been material in relation to the Company&#x2019;s financial position, results of operations, or cash flows. These risks could increase, however, as the Company expands in international markets and markets becomes more volatile. The Company estimates that a 10% and 20% adverse change in the underlying foreign currency exchange rates would have decreased reported net income in fiscal 201</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;"> by approximately $</font><font style="display: inline;">0.</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;"> million and $1.</font><font style="display: inline;">1</font><font style="display: inline;"> million, respectively. Historically, the Company believes that adverse changes in foreign exchange rates have not materially impacted its financial condition.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">The Company is subject to interest rate risk related to borrowings under the credit facility. The variable rate identified is based on L</font><font style="display: inline;">IBOR plus a calculated margin. </font><font style="display: inline;">S</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">ee Note 1</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">0</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> to the Consolidated Financial Statements</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">for additional</font><font style="display: inline;"> information regar</font><font style="display: inline;">ding </font><font style="display: inline;">the credit facility.</font>

In connection with our audits of the financial statements, we have also audited the financial statement schedule listed in the accompanying index. These financial statements are the responsibility of the Company&#x2019;s management.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our responsibility is to express an opinion on these financial statements based on our audits.</font>

An audit also includes examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the consolidated financial statements, assessing the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall presentation of the consolidated financial statements and schedule.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">The consolidated financial statements </font><font style="display: inline;">have been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;">U.S. GAAP&#x201D;) and </font><font style="display: inline;">include the accounts of the Company</font><font style="display: inline;"> and</font><font style="display: inline;"> its subsidiaries. All intercompany balances and transactions </font><font style="display: inline;">have been </font><font style="display: inline;">eliminated in consolidation. Entities in which the Company does not have a controlling financial interest</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> but is considered to have significant influence</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> are accounted for on the equity method.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Use of Estimates</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The preparation of financial statements in conformity with </font><font style="display: inline;">U.S. GAAP</font><font style="display: inline;"> requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the </font><font style="display: inline;">consolidated </font><font style="display: inline;">financial statements and the reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting period. Actual results could differ from those estimates.</font>
		</p>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Cash and cash equivalents include </font><font style="display: inline;">all unrestricted </font><font style="display: inline;">cash and </font><font style="display: inline;">highly liquid </font><font style="display: inline;">investments with an original maturity of three months or less</font><font style="display: inline;">,</font><font style="display: inline;"> primarily short-term money market instruments.</font>

We continuously monitor aging reports, collections and payments from customers, and a provision for estimated credit losses is maintained based upon </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;color:#000000;">the Company&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;color:#000000;"> historical experience and any specific customer collection issues that have been identified. While such credit losses have historically been within our expectations and the provisions established, we cannot guarantee that the same credit loss rates will be experienced in the future. </font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;color:#000000;">The Company</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;color:#000000;"> write</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;color:#000000;">s</font><font style="display: inline;font-family:inherit;color:#000000;"> off accounts receivable when they are determined to be uncollectible.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Long-lived assets, including definite-lived intangible assets, are reviewed for impairment whenever events or changes in business circumstances indicate that the carrying value of the assets may not be fully recoverable. The Company performs undiscounted operating cash flow analyses to determine if an impairment exists. For purposes of recognition and measurement of an impairment for assets held for use, the Company groups assets and liabilities at the lowest level for which cash flows are separately identifiable. If an impairment is determined to exist, any related impairment loss is calculated based on fair value. Impairment losses on assets to be disposed of, if any, are based on the estimated proceeds to be received, less costs of disposal. The Company also reviews the estimated remaining useful lives of long-lived assets whenever events or changes in business circumstances indicate the lives may have changed.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Equity in Joint Ventures</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Entities in which the Company does not have a controlling financial interest but is considered to have significant influence are accounted for on the equity method. Under the equity method, a company records its share of net income or loss of an investment based on its percentage ownership. </font><font style="display: inline;">Additional information regarding the Company&#x2019;s equity in joint ventures is contained in Note </font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Goodwill and other indefinite-lived intangible assets must be assessed for impairment annually or more frequently if events or changes in circumstances indicate that such assets might be impaired. Triggering events include, but are not limited to a current period operating or cash flow loss; a product, technology or service introduced by a competitor; or a loss of key personnel.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Goodwill impairment testing first requires a comparison between the carrying value and fair value of a reporting unit with associated goodwill. Carrying value is based on the assets and liabilities associated with the operations of that reporting unit. The Company estimates the fair value of the reporting units using the income approach and the market approach. If the Company believes that the fair value of a reporting unit exceeds its carrying value by a substantial margin, the Company may perform a qualitative analysis instead.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:110%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">If the fair value of a </font><font style="display: inline;">reporting unit</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">exceeds its carrying amount, goodwill of the </font><font style="display: inline;">reporting unit</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">is considered not to be impaired and the second step of the impairment test is unnecessary. If the carrying amount of the </font><font style="display: inline;">reporting unit</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">exceeds its fair value, the second step of the goodwill impairment test is performed to measure the amount of the impairment loss, if any. The second step of the goodwill impairment test compares the implied fair value of the </font><font style="display: inline;">reporting unit&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">goodwill with the carrying amount of that goodwill. If the carrying amount of the </font><font style="display: inline;">reporting unit&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">goodwill exceeds the implied fair value of that goodwill, an impairment loss is recognized in an amount equal to that excess. The implied fair value of goodwill is determined in the same manner as the amount of goodwill recognized in a business combination. That is, the fair value of the </font><font style="display: inline;">reporting unit</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">is allocated to all of the assets and liabilities of that unit (including any unrecognized intangible assets) as if the </font><font style="display: inline;">reporting unit</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">had been acquired in a business combination, and the fair value of the </font><font style="display: inline;">reporting unit</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">was the purchase price paid to acquire the segment.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The impairment test for an indefinite-lived intangible asset other than goodwill consist</font><font style="display: inline;">s</font><font style="display: inline;"> of first assessing qualitative factors, such as company, industry and economic trends. If determined to be necessary, the next step compares the fair value of the intangible asset to its carrying amount. If the carrying amount exceeds the fair value, an impairment loss is recognized for the difference.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Additional information regarding the Company&#x2019;s goodwill and other intangible assets is contained in Note </font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>

The Company views its business in the Radiation Measurement segment as services provided to customers over a period of time and the wear period is the period over which those services are provided. Badge production, wearing of badges, badge analysis, and report preparation are integral to the benefit that the Company provides to its customers. 		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company measures and recognizes compensation cost at fair value</font><font style="display: inline;"> as of the grant date</font><font style="display: inline;"> for all share-based payments, including stock options. </font>

			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company has not granted stock options subsequent to fiscal 2005. Awards of stock options in prior fiscal years were granted with an exercise price equal to the market value of the stock on the date of grant. The fair value of stock options was estimated using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model. Expected volatility and the expected life of stock options were based on historical experience. The risk free interest rate was derived from the implied yield available on U.S. Treasury zero-coupon issues with a remaining term, as of the date of grant, equal to the expected term of the option. The dividend yield was based on annual dividends and the fair market value of the Company&#x2019;s stock on the date of grant. Compensation expense was recognized ratably over the vesting period of the stock option.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Subsequent to fiscal 2005, key employees and/or non-employee directors have been granted restricted share awards that consist of performance shares and time vested restricted stock. Performance shares represent a right to receive shares of common stock upon satisfaction of performance goals or other specified metrics. Restricted stock represents a right to receive shares of common stock upon the passage of a specified period of time. </font><font style="display: inline;">T</font><font style="display: inline;">he fair value of performance shares and restricted stock is based on the Company&#x2019;s closing stock price on the date of grant. Compensation expense for performance shares is recorded ratably over the vesting period, assuming that achievement of performance goals is deemed probable. Compensation expense for restricted stock is cliff vested and recognized ra</font><font style="display: inline;">tably over the vesting period. </font><font style="display: inline;">The Company also retains the discretion to make additional awards to executives at other times for rec</font><font style="display: inline;">ruiting or retention purposes. </font><font style="display: inline;">Stock-based compensation for these awards can be either cliff or graded vested depending on the agreement, and recognized ratably over the vesting period</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Forfeitures of awards are estimated at the time of grant and stock-based compensation cost is recognized only for </font><font style="display: inline;">those awards expected to vest. </font><font style="display: inline;">The Company uses historical experience to e</font><font style="display: inline;">stimate projected forfeitures. </font><font style="display: inline;">The Company recognizes the cumulative effect on current and prior periods of a change in the forfeiture rate, or actual </font><font style="display: inline;">forfeitures, as compensation cost or as a reduction of cost in the period of the revision.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Foreign Currency Translation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Financial statements of foreign subsidiaries are translated into U.S. dollars using period-end exchange rates for assets and liabilities and weighted-average exchange rates for revenues and expenses. Adjustments resulting from translating net assets are reported as a separate component of accumulated other comprehensive loss within common shareholders&#x2019; equity as currency translation adjustment.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Recent Accounting Pronouncements</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;text-decoration:underline;">Accounting Standards Not Yet Adopted</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:6pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In May 2014, the </font><font style="display: inline;">Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;">FASB</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201D;)</font><font style="display: inline;"> issued new guidance for recognizing revenue from contracts with customers, which provides a single comprehensive model for entities to use in accounting for revenue arising from contracts with customers and will supersede most curren</font><font style="display: inline;">t revenue recognition guidance.</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">In July 2015, the FASB deferred the effective date of the new revenue standard by one year. Public companies would now be required to adopt the new guidance for fiscal years, and interim periods within those fiscal years, beginning after December 15, 2017. The FASB decided to allow earlier adoption of the new revenue standard, but not earlier than the original effective date. </font><font style="display: inline;">This guidance is effective for the Company in th</font><font style="display: inline;">e first quarter of fiscal 201</font><font style="display: inline;">9</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;"> The Company is currently evaluating the impact this guidance will have on its </font><font style="display: inline;">results of operations, financial position and liquidity</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;To date, the Company has formed a committee to evaluate the impact and are in the initial stages of evaluation.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;"></font><font style="display: inline;">51</font><font style="display: inline;"></font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			&nbsp;

		</p>

</div><hr size="3" style="color:#999999" width="100%" align="center"></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">In June 2014, the FASB issued new guidance on accounting for share-based payments requiring a specific performance target to be achieved in order for employees to become eligible to vest in the awards when that performance target may be achieved after the requisite</font><font style="display: inline;"> service period for the award. </font><font style="display: inline;">This update further clarifies that compensation cost should be recognized in the period in which it becomes probable that the performance target will be achieved and should represent the compensation cost attributable to the period for which the requisite ser</font><font style="display: inline;">vice has already been rendered.</font><font style="display: inline;"> This guidance is effective for the Company in the</font><font style="display: inline;"> first quarter of fiscal 201</font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;">. Early adoption is permitted. </font><font style="display: inline;">The Company </font><font style="display: inline;">has evaluated</font><font style="display: inline;"> the impact this guidance will have on its</font><font style="display: inline;"> results of operations, financial position and liquidity</font><font style="display: inline;"> and has concluded that the impact is </font><font style="display: inline;">nominal</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">In April 2015, the FASB issued new guidance on the presentation of debt issuance costs. This update requires a company to present debt issuance costs related to a recognized debt liability </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">i</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">n the balance sheet as a </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">direct </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">d</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">eduction from the carrying amount of the related debt liability</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, consistent with the presentation of debt discounts. Currently, debt issuance costs are</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">presented as a deferred</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> asset. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The recognition and measurement requirements will not change as a result of this guidance</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">. The update requires retrospective application and represents a cha</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">nge in accounting principle. This guidance </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">is effective for </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">the Company in the first quarter of fiscal 2017, with early adoption permitted</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> The Company does not expect the adoption of this guidance will have a material impact on its results of operations, financial position</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">and</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">liquidity</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In April 2015, the FASB issued new guidance on a customer&#x2019;s accounting for fees paid in a cloud computing arrangement (CCA).&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the new standard, customers will apply the same criteria as vendors to determine whether a CCA contains a software license or is solely a service contract.&nbsp;&nbsp;This standard is effective for the Company in the first quarter of fiscal 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company </font><font style="display: inline;">has evaluated </font><font style="display: inline;">the impact this guidance will have on its results of operations, financial position and liquidity</font><font style="display: inline;"> and has concluded that the impact is no</font><font style="display: inline;">minal</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">In July 2015, the FASB issued new guidance on simplifying the measurement of inventory. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">This</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> update requires a company to measure inventory at the lower of cost and net realizable value. Net realizable value is the estimated selling prices in the ordinary course of business, less reasonably predictable costs of completion, disposal, and transportation. </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">This guidance is effective for the Company in the first quarter of fis</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">cal 2018</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, and should be applied prospectively with early adoption permitted. The Company is currently evaluating the impact this guidance will have on its</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">results of operations, financial position</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">and</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">liquidity</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">In November 2015, the FASB issued new guidance on the presentation of deferred income taxes. This update requires a company to present </font><font style="display: inline;">deferred tax liabilities and assets as noncurrent in a classified statement of financial position</font><font style="display: inline;"> rather than the current requirement to separate deferred income tax liabilities and assets into current and noncurrent amounts</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">This guidance is effective for the Company in </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">the first quarter of fiscal 201</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">8</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">, with early adoption permitted.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;"> The Company does not expect the adoption of this guidance will have a material impact on its results of operations, financial position</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">and</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">liquidity</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In February 2016, the FASB issued guidance on the accounting treatment for leases.&nbsp;&nbsp;This guidance will require all leases with durations greater than twelve months to be recognized on the balance sheet of the lessee.&nbsp;&nbsp;For income statement purposes, the FASB retained a dual model, requiring leases to be classified as either operating or finance.&nbsp;&nbsp;Classification will be based on criteria that are largely similar to those applied in current lease accounting, but without explicit bright lines.&nbsp;&nbsp;This guidance is effective for the Company in the first quarter of fiscal 2020, although early adoption is permitted.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is currently evaluating the impact that adoption of this guidance will have on its results of operations, financial position and liquidity.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In March 2016, the FASB issued new guidance to improve the accounting for share-based payments.&nbsp;&nbsp;This standard makes several modifications to Topic 718 related to the accounting for forfeitures, employer tax withholding on share-based compensation and the financial statement presentation of excess tax benefits or deficiencies.&nbsp;&nbsp;The guidance also clarifies the statement of cash flows presentation for certain components of share-based awards.&nbsp;&nbsp;The standard is effective for the Company in the first quarter of fiscal 2018, although early adoption is permitted.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is currently evaluating the impact that adoption of this guidance will have on its results of operations, financial position and liquidity.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">In June 2016, the FASB issued new guidance to </font><font style="display: inline;">introduce a new model for recognizing credit losses on financial instruments based on an estimate of current expected credit losses.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">The update replaces the incurred loss impairment methodology in current GAAP with a methodology that reflects expected credit losses and requires consideration of a broader range of reasonable and supportable information to inform credit loss estimates.&nbsp;&nbsp;The update is effective for the Company in the first quarter of fiscal 2020, although early adoption is permitted.&nbsp; The Company is currently evaluating the effect that this update will have on its financial statements and related disclosures. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">In August 2016, the FASB issued guidance related to the </font><font style="display: inline;">presentation and classification of certain transactions in the </font><font style="display: inline;">Statement of Cash Flows</font><font style="display: inline;"> where diversity in practice exists, making</font><font style="display: inline;"> targeted changes to how cash receipts and cash payments are presented in the statement of cash flows.&nbsp;&nbsp;The update is effective for the Company is the first quarter of fiscal 2018.&nbsp; The Company is&nbsp;currently evaluating the effect that this update will have on its financial statements and related disclosures. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

			<font style="display: inline;">No other new accounting pronouncement issued or effective during the fiscal year had, or is expected to have, a material impact on the Consolidated Financial Statements.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;punctuation-wrap:hanging;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;vertical-align:baseline;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">2</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;;font-size: 11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 36pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;"></font><a name="FairValueMeasurements"></a><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">Fair Value Measurements</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;punctuation-wrap:hanging;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;vertical-align:baseline;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The Company</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">estimates</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">the</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">fair value</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">of</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">assets and liabilities</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">in accordance with</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">the framework established</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">by</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">the</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">authoritative guidance for fair value measurements. The framework is based on the inputs used in valuation, gives the highest priority to quoted prices in active markets and requires that observable inputs be used in</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">the valuations when available. The disclosure of fair value estimates in the fair value accounting guidance hierarchy is based on whether the significant inputs into the valuation are observable.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">In determining the level of the hierarchy in which the estimate is disclosed, the highest priority is given to unadjusted quoted prices in active markets and the lowest priority to unobservable inputs that reflect the Company&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">significant market assumptions.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The level in the fair value hierarchy within which the fair value measurement is reported is based on the lowest level input that is significant to the measurement in its entirety.</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">The three levels of the hierarchy are as follows:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#xFEFF;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">Level </font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">1</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&#x2013; Unadjusted</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">quoted prices in active markets for identical assets</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">or</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">liabilities</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">that the Company has the ability to access</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">as of the reporting date</font><font style="display: inline;color:#000000;">.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>

The Company recognized a </font><font style="display: inline;">$1.0</font><font style="display: inline;"> million pre-tax gain on sale from the disposition of this business. In conjunction with this transaction, the Company released </font><font style="display: inline;">$1.4</font><font style="display: inline;"> million of foreign currency translation losses previously recorded in accumulated other comprehensive loss, resulting in a </font><font style="display: inline;">$0.4</font><font style="display: inline;"> million net loss on the disposition of business. The Company has evaluated whether this divestiture qualifies as a discontinued operation pursuant to FASB Accounting Standards Codification 205-20 &#x201C;Discontinued Operations.&#x201D; The Company has concluded that the transaction should not be reported as a discontinued operation and is not material to the Company&#x2019;s financial results.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;punctuation-wrap:hanging;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;vertical-align:baseline;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">5</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">.</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;;font-size: 11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 36pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;"></font><a name="EPS"></a><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">Income </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">(Loss) </font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">per Common Share</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;punctuation-wrap:hanging;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;vertical-align:baseline;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Basic net</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">income </font><font style="display: inline;">(loss)</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">per share was computed by dividing net</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">income </font><font style="display: inline;">(loss)</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">available to common stockholders for the period by the weighted average number of shares of common stock outstanding during the period. Diluted net income </font><font style="display: inline;">(loss) </font><font style="display: inline;">per share was computed by dividing net income</font><font style="display: inline;"> (loss)</font><font style="display: inline;"> available to common stockholders for the period by the weighted average number of shares of common stock that would have been outstanding assuming dilution from stock-based compensation awards during the period.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;;font-size: 10pt"><font style="display: inline;">The effective tax rates for the fiscal years ended September 30, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;">, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">5</font><font style="display: inline;"> and 201</font><font style="display: inline;">4</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">were</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">34.9</font><font style="display: inline;">%</font><font style="display: inline;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">29.4</font><font style="display: inline;">%</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">39.0%</font><font style="display: inline;">, respectively. </font><font style="display: inline;">The </font><font style="display: inline;">in</font><font style="display: inline;">crease in the fiscal 201</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;"> effective tax rate was primarily due to the mix of earnings between jurisdictions with differing tax rates and the </font><font style="display: inline;">valuation allowance recorded to offset the tax impact of capital losses generated from divestitures.</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">The following is a reconciliation of the</font><font style="display: inline;"> U.S. federal statutory rate of </font><font style="display: inline;">35.0</font><font style="display: inline;">% to the effective income tax rate:</font>
		</p>

The Company believes that the realization of this deferred tax assets is more likely than not based upon the expectation</font><font style="display: inline;"> that</font><font style="display: inline;"> the Company will generate the necessary taxable income in the future periods. Therefore, </font><font style="display: inline;">no</font><font style="display: inline;"> valuation allowance w</font><font style="display: inline;">as</font><font style="display: inline;"> recorded for this deferred tax asset.</font>

In recognition of this risk, the Company has recorde</font><font style="display: inline;">d a valuation allowance of </font><font style="display: inline;">$456</font><font style="display: inline;"> against th</font><font style="display: inline;">e</font><font style="display: inline;"> deferred tax asset</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display: inline;">As of September 30, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;">, the Company</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;">s U.S. income tax returns for fiscal 201</font><font style="display: inline;">3</font><font style="display: inline;"> and subsequent years remained subject to examination by the Internal Revenue Service (</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201C;</font><font style="display: inline;">IRS</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x201D;</font><font style="display: inline;">). </font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">State income tax returns generally have statute of limitations for periods between </font><font style="display: inline;">three</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">four</font><font style="display: inline;"> years from the date of filing. The Company is currently undergoing a state income tax audit. The Company does not expect the audit to have a material impact on its consolidated financial statements. The Company is not currently under audit in any foreign jurisdictions. The Company&#x2019;s foreign operations have statute of limitations on the examination of tax returns for periods between </font><font style="display: inline;">two</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">six</font><font style="display: inline;"> years.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company operates in numerous taxing jurisdictions and is subject to regular examinations by various U.S. federal, state, local and foreign jurisdictions for various tax periods. The Company&#x2019;s income tax positions are based on research and interpretations of the income tax laws and rulings in each of the jurisdictions in which it does business. Due to the subjectivity of interpretations of the income tax laws and rulings in each jurisdiction, the differences and interplay in tax laws between those jurisdictions, as well as the inherent uncertainty in estimating the final resolution of complex tax audit matters, the Company&#x2019;s estimates of income tax liabilities may differ from actual payments or assessments.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Accounting for uncertainty in income taxes requires a more-likely-than-not threshold for financial statement recognition and measurement of tax positions taken or expected to be taken in a tax return. The Company records a liability for the difference between the benefit recognized and measured for financial statement purposes and the tax position taken or expected to be taken on its tax return. To the extent that the Company&#x2019;s assessment of such tax positions changes, the change in estimate is recorded in the period in which the determination is made.</font>

Cash dividends of $</font><font style="display: inline;">1</font><font style="display: inline;">.100</font><font style="display: inline;"> per common share were declared in fiscal </font><font style="display: inline;">year </font><font style="display: inline;">201</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;">. As of September 30, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;">, there were accrued and unpaid dividends of $</font><font style="display: inline;">2,</font><font style="display: inline;">815</font><font style="display: inline;">. The Company has reserved </font><font style="display: inline;">7</font><font style="display: inline;">00,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares of common stock under the </font><font style="display: inline;">2016 </font><font style="display: inline;">Landauer, Inc. Incentive Compensation Plan approved by shareholders on February </font><font style="display: inline;">18</font><font style="display: inline;">, 20</font><font style="display: inline;">16</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;Previously, Landauer had reserved </font><font style="display: inline;">500,000</font><font style="display: inline;"> shares of common stock for grants under its</font><font style="display: inline;"> Landauer, Inc. Incentive Compen</font><font style="display: inline;">sation Plan.&nbsp;&nbsp;Upon approval of the new plan in 2016, all shares reserved under the prior plan were cancelled.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;punctuation-wrap:hanging;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;vertical-align:baseline;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 11pt">
			<font style="text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt; padding-right:15.5pt;"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">1</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">2</font><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">.</font></font><font style="text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt; padding-right:4pt;text-align:left"><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;"></font><a name="EmployeeBenefitPlans"></a><font style="display: inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;">Employee Benefit Plans</font></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;punctuation-wrap:hanging;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;vertical-align:baseline;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company sponsors postretirement benefit plans to provide pension, supplemental retirement funds, and medical expense reimbursement to eligible retired employees, as well as a directors&#x2019; retirement plan that provides for certain retirement benefits payable to non-employee directors. Following is a description of these benefit plans.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Defined Contribution Plans&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company </font><font style="display: inline;">sponsors</font><font style="display: inline;"> a 401(k) </font><font style="display: inline;">retirement </font><font style="display: inline;">savings plan covering substantially all Radiation Measurement U.S. full-time employees</font><font style="display: inline;"> as well as substantially</font><font style="display: inline;"> all of the employees of the Company&#x2019;s Medical Physics </font><font style="display: inline;">segment and, prior to its divestiture, the</font><font style="display: inline;"> Medical Products segment. The Company also maintains a supplemental defined contribution plan for certain executives, which allows participating executives to make voluntary deferrals and provides for employer contributions at the</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">Company</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;s</font><font style="display: inline;"> discretion. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The plans are qualified under applicable sections of the Internal Revenue Code and allow employees to contribute a portion of their pre-tax income in accordance with specified guidelines. The Company matches a percentage of the employee contributions up to certain limits. </font><font style="display: inline;">Amounts expensed for Company contributions under these plans during the fiscal years ended September 30, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;">, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">5</font><font style="display: inline;"> and 201</font><font style="display: inline;">4</font><font style="display: inline;"> were </font><font style="display: inline;">$1,</font><font style="display: inline;">842</font><font style="display: inline;">, $</font><font style="display: inline;">1,7</font><font style="display: inline;">84</font><font style="display: inline;"> and $</font><font style="display: inline;">1,</font><font style="display: inline;">723</font><font style="display: inline;">, respectively. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;font-style:italic;">Defined Benefit Plans</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Historically the Company provided, to substantially all full-time employees in the U.S., a qualified noncontributory defined benefit pension plan to provide a basic replacement income benefit upon retirement. For key executives, the basic benefit was </font><font style="display: inline;">augmented</font><font style="display: inline;"> with a supplemental executive retirement plan to address U.S. tax law limitations placed on the benefits under the qualified pension plan. The supplemental plan is not separately funded and costs of the plan are expensed annually. The qualified noncontributory defined benefit pension plan and the supplemental executive retirement plan were frozen in fiscal 2009 and future benefit accruals under such plans ceased. The Company formerly maintained a directors</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;"> retirement plan that provide</font><font style="display: inline;">d</font><font style="display: inline;"> certain retirement benefits for non-employee directors. The directors</font><font style="display: inline;">&#x2019;</font><font style="display: inline;"> plan was terminated in January 1997 and benefits accrued under the retirement plan </font><font style="display: inline;">we</font><font style="display: inline;">re frozen.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company also maintains an unfunded retiree medical expense reimbursement plan. Under the terms of the plan, which covers retirees with </font><font style="display: inline;">ten</font><font style="display: inline;"> or more years of service, the Company reimburses retirees to age 70, or to age 65 in accordance with plan changes effective October 1, 2005, for (i) a portion of the cost of coverage under the then-current medical and dental insurance plans if the retiree is under age 65, or (ii) all or a portion of the cost of Medicare and supplemental coverage if the retiree is over age 64. The assumptions for health-care cost ultimate trend rates were </font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;">% for those younger than 65, and </font><font style="display: inline;">5</font><font style="display: inline;">% for those 65 and older.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:normal;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company recognizes the over- or underfunded status of its defined benefit pension and postretirement plans on its balance sheet and recognizes changes in the funded status, as the changes occur, through comprehensive income. The Company uses its fiscal year end, September</font><font style="display: inline;"> 30, as the measurement date for its plans. The following tables set forth the status of the combined defined benefit pension plans and the postretirement medical plan, as pension benefits and other benefits, respectively, at September 30.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display: inline;">The weighted-average discount rate used to determine benefit obligations at September&nbsp;30, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;"> was </font><font style="display: inline;">3.38%,</font><font style="display: inline;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">3.</font><font style="display: inline;">04</font><font style="display: inline;">%</font><font style="display: inline;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">3.30</font><font style="display: inline;">%</font><font style="display: inline;"> and </font><font style="display: inline;">2.</font><font style="display: inline;">35</font><font style="display: inline;">%</font><font style="display: inline;"> for Pension, Key Executive SERP, Manager SERP and Directors plans, respectively, which all fall under &#x201C;Pension Benefits&#x201D; in this footnote. The weighted-average discount rate used to determine benefit obligations under &#x201C;Other Benefits&#x201D; was </font><font style="display: inline;">2.76</font><font style="display: inline;">%</font><font style="display: inline;"> at September</font><font style="display: inline;"> 30, 201</font><font style="display: inline;">6</font><font style="display: inline;">.</font>
		</p>

				<td valign="bottom" style="width:16.32%;border-top:1pt solid #000000 ;border-left:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:2pt double #000000 ;border-right:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;height:12.75pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-align:right;" nowrap="nowrap">100%&nbsp;
				</td>

		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">Plan assets for the qualified defined benefit pension plan include marketable equity securities, corporate and government debt securities, and cash and short-term investments. The plan assets are not directly invested in the Company&#x2019;s common stock. The supplemental executive retirement plans and the directors&#x2019; retirement plan are not separately funded.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The plan&#x2019;s investment strategy supports the objectives of the plan. These objectives are to maximize returns in order to meet long-term cash requirements within reasonable and prudent levels of risk. To achieve these objectives, the Company has established a strategic asset allocation policy which is to maintain approximately one </font><font style="display: inline;">half</font><font style="display: inline;"> of plan assets in high quality fixed income securities such as investment grade bonds and short</font><font style="display: inline;">-</font><font style="display: inline;">term government securities, with the other </font><font style="display: inline;">half</font><font style="display: inline;"> containing large capitalization equity securities. The plan&#x2019;s objective is to periodically rebalance its assets to approximate weighted-average target asset allocations. Investments are diversified across classes and within each class to minimize the risk of large losses.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>

Plan assets measured at fair value on a recurring basis are summarized below:</font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">During fiscal 2014, t</font><font style="display: inline;">he Company changed the presentation of its reporting segments to separately disclose certain &#x2018;corporate expenses&#x2019; that had previously been reported within the </font><font style="display: inline;">Radiation Measurement segment. </font><font style="display: inline;">As a result, the current segment disclosures reflect </font><font style="display: inline;">three</font><font style="display: inline;"> reporting segments </font><font style="display: inline;">(</font><font style="display: inline;">Radiation Measurement, Medical Physics and Medical Products</font><font style="display: inline;">)</font><font style="display: inline;"> and one functional group</font><font style="display: inline;"> &nbsp;(</font><font style="display: inline;">Corporate</font><font style="display: inline;">)</font><font style="display: inline;">. &nbsp;</font><font style="display: inline;">As disclosed in Note 4 to the Consolidated Financial Statements, Medical Products was divested in May 2016 which resulted in a reduction in revenues, operating income, depreciation and amortization and the elimination of assets for the year ended September 30, 2016.&nbsp; </font><font style="display: inline;">The factors for determining the reportable segments reflect specific markets and the products and services offered combined with the nature of the individual business traits, as well as key financial information reviewed by management. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Radiation Measurement segment provides analytical services to determine occupational and environmental radiation exposure. These services are provided internationally primarily to hospitals, medical and dental offices, universities, national laboratories, and nuclear facilities. Radiation Measurement activities include the manufacture of various types of radiation detection monitors, the distribution and collection of the monitors to and from customers, and the analysis and reporting of exposure findings. In addition to providing analytical services, the Radiation Measurement segment sells dosimetry detectors and reading equipment.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Medical Physics segment provides therapeutic and imaging physics services to domestic hospitals and radiation therapy centers. Service offerings include clinical physics support, equipment commissioning, accreditation support and imaging equipment testing. These professional services are provided to customers on-site by skilled physicists. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Medical Products segment provide</font><font style="display: inline;">d</font><font style="display: inline;"> medical consumable accessories used in radiology, radiation therapy, and image guided surgery procedures. Medical products range</font><font style="display: inline;">d</font><font style="display: inline;"> from consumables used with MRI, CT, and mammography technologies to highly engineered passive reflective markers used during image guided surgery procedures. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">The Company</font><font style="display: inline;"> primarily evaluates performance of the individual segments based upon, among other metrics, segment operating income or loss. Segment operating income or loss is segment revenues less segment cost of sales and segment selling, general and administrative expenses. Corporate expenses for shared functions, including corporate management, corporate finance and human resources, are recognized in the Corporate functional group. In addition, acquisition and reorganization costs are not allocated to the segments. Information about net other income, including interest income and expense, and income taxes is not provided at the segment level. As the Company&#x2019;s business model evolves in increased complexity, management may determine it necessary to change this reporting practice to reflect any appropriate allocations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;line-height:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size: 10pt">
			<font style="display: inline;">&#xFEFF;</font>
		</p>
